questions.prompt: The new rail line is expected to ___ travel times between the two cities.
questions.rationale: ‘reduce travel times’ is the natural collocation.

questions.prompt: The results should be treated with ___ because the study included only 18 participants.
questions.rationale: ‘treated with caution’ means interpreted carefully.

questions.prompt: In the sentence ‘The policy had a negligible effect on overall demand’, negligible most nearly means:
questions.rationale: Negligible means too small to be important.

questions.prompt: Choose the most natural phrase:
questions.rationale: ‘heavy rain’ is the standard collocation.

questions.prompt: The university introduced extra tutorials to ___ students who were struggling with statistics.
questions.rationale: ‘support students’ fits the context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best paraphrases ‘The proposal was rejected primarily because of its cost’?
options: Cost was the main reason the proposal was rejected.
The proposal reduced the expected cost.
The proposal was rejected before its cost was known.
Cost was one of several equally important reasons.
questions.answer: Cost was the main reason the proposal was rejected.
questions.rationale: ‘primarily’ means mainly.

questions.prompt: By the time the meeting started, the research team ___ the revised figures.
questions.rationale: Past perfect marks an earlier completed past action.

questions.prompt: Choose the most natural sentence.
options: The number of applicants have increased.
The number of applicants has increased.
The number of applicant have increased.
questions.answer: The number of applicants has increased.
questions.rationale: The subject is singular: ‘the number’.

questions.prompt: The library, ___ was renovated last year, now stays open until midnight.
questions.rationale: A non-defining relative clause uses ‘which’ for a thing.

questions.prompt: Although the initial results were promising, ___ .
options: the researchers decided to collect more data
but the researchers decided to collect more data
the data because more were needed
questions.answer: the researchers decided to collect more data
questions.rationale: ‘Although’ already marks contrast; no extra ‘but’ is needed.

questions.prompt: Choose the most natural article use.
options: Access to the reliable public transport can affect employment opportunities.
Access to reliable public transport can affect employment opportunities.
An access to reliable public transport can affect the employment opportunities generally.
The access to a reliable public transport can affect employment opportunity.
questions.answer: Access to reliable public transport can affect employment opportunities.
questions.rationale: General uncountable/abstract nouns take zero article here.

questions.prompt: If the city ___ more protected cycle lanes, more commuters might consider cycling.
questions.rationale: Second conditional pattern: if + past, might/would + base.

sections.name: Reading
sections.passage:
For many years, city planners treated public benches as simple pieces of street furniture. More recent research, however, suggests that where benches are placed can affect how people use public space. A seat beside a busy road may be technically available but unattractive because of noise and pollution. By contrast, a bench with shade, a clear view, and some distance from traffic may encourage people to stop for longer.

This matters because staying in a public space is different from merely passing through it. When people have comfortable places to sit, older residents can rest during a walk, parents can pause with children, and neighbours have more opportunities for informal conversation. In this sense, a bench can support social contact even though it does not create a community by itself.

Placement also affects accessibility. A long pedestrian route may be manageable for a fit adult but difficult for someone with limited mobility if there is nowhere to rest. For this reason, some planners look at the distance between seats rather than only the total number installed. A neighbourhood with twenty benches concentrated in one park may provide less practical support than a neighbourhood with fewer benches distributed along common walking routes.

There are limits to what design can achieve. A well-placed bench will not make an unsafe area feel welcoming, and seating that blocks narrow paths may create problems for wheelchair users. Maintenance matters too: damaged or dirty seating is unlikely to be used. The broader lesson is that small pieces of infrastructure should be judged by how they fit into everyday behaviour, not simply by whether they are present.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the first paragraph?
options: The usefulness of a bench depends partly on its location.
Shade is the most important feature of public space.
questions.answer: The usefulness of a bench depends partly on its location.
questions.rationale: The paragraph contrasts technically available seating with seating people are more likely to use.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, comfortable seating can help public spaces by:
questions.rationale: The passage says seating creates more opportunities for informal conversation.

questions.prompt: Why does the writer compare twenty benches in one park with fewer benches along walking routes?
options: To show that distribution can matter more than total quantity
To argue that parks should have no benches
To show that fit adults need more seating
To prove that benches are too expensive
questions.answer: To show that distribution can matter more than total quantity
questions.rationale: The paragraph focuses on accessibility and spacing.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 3, ‘manageable’ most nearly means:
questions.rationale: The route may be possible for one person but difficult for another.

questions.prompt: Which statement is supported by paragraph 4?
options: Good design can solve every problem in a public space.
Benches should never be placed on narrow paths.
Maintenance and surrounding conditions influence whether seating is useful.
Wheelchair users prefer parks to streets.
questions.answer: Maintenance and surrounding conditions influence whether seating is useful.
questions.rationale: The paragraph mentions safety, blocked paths, damage and cleanliness.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's overall conclusion?
options: Small infrastructure should be evaluated in relation to real human behaviour.
Public benches are more important than public transport.
Every neighbourhood should have the same number of benches.
Urban design research focuses too much on behaviour.
questions.answer: Small infrastructure should be evaluated in relation to real human behaviour.
questions.rationale: This restates the final sentence and the passage's central message.

sections.name: Listening
sections.transcript:
Hello everyone. Before we start tomorrow's field trip, I need to make two changes to the schedule. We originally planned to meet outside the science building at eight thirty, but the entrance there will be closed for maintenance. Please meet at the main library entrance instead. The time is unchanged: eight thirty.

We will travel to the coastal research centre by coach. Some of you asked whether you could take the train and meet us there, but the centre is about twenty minutes from the nearest station, so please use the coach unless you have already spoken to me about a different arrangement.

Bring a notebook and a waterproof jacket. You do not need to bring lunch because the centre will provide sandwiches and fruit. If you have a dietary requirement and you haven't told the department yet, send me a message before four o'clock today.

The weather forecast has improved, so the outdoor sampling activity will probably go ahead. However, the beach can be windy even when it is dry. We should return to campus at about five fifteen, although heavy traffic could make us slightly late.

questions.prompt: Where should students meet?
questions.rationale: The original science-building location changed because of maintenance.

questions.prompt: What time should they meet?
questions.rationale: The location changed, but the time was unchanged.

questions.prompt: Why are students asked to use the coach?
options: The centre is not close to the station.
The coach is free only tomorrow.
questions.answer: The centre is not close to the station.
questions.rationale: It is about twenty minutes from the nearest station.

questions.prompt: What do students NOT need to bring?
questions.rationale: The centre will provide sandwiches and fruit.

questions.prompt: When must unreported dietary requirements be sent?
questions.rationale: The speaker gives a clear deadline.

questions.prompt: What may affect the return time?
questions.rationale: The speaker says heavy traffic could make them slightly late.

guardrails: Do not report an official or exact IELTS band from this test.
If any section score is 0-2, include that section in Best Next Opportunities even when total score is high.
If section scores differ by 3 or more points, label the profile 'uneven' and use skill-specific recommendations.
A 23-24 score is only a strong starting signal; it does not establish C1 proficiency.
Update placement after at least 3 completed lessons or a fuller diagnostic.

confidence.High: All 24 items completed; no section omitted; section scores are not extremely uneven.
confidence.Moderate: All sections completed but profile is uneven, or 1-2 items unanswered.
confidence.Low: A section is omitted, audio could not be completed, or 3+ items are unanswered.
